clue.text: Handy expressions of approval

parts.note: praise given by the hands: clapping, the original sense of applause

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' here means made with the hands, not convenient: the approval is clapped rather than spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaudits are expressions of praise, literally rounds of applause from clapping hands.

clue.text: Timber producer of high standing until found to be heartless

indicators.note: the central letter, the heart, is taken out of the word for being well thought of

parts.note: popular means well liked, held in high regard

explanation.surface: A tree, prized only until it is found to have no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle U of POPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tree, and trees are what timber comes from.

clue.text: A southern university river rises where Francis came from

indicators.note: in a down clue the river rises, so its name is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A river near a southern university rises at Francis's birthplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses ISIS to SISI.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Francis is named after the Umbrian town where he was born.

clue.text: Told he can become involved in an Olympic event

indicators.note: the words told he can become involved, entangled, so their letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An athlete is told he can take part in an event at the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-event athletics contest is one of the Olympic disciplines.

clue.text: They provided new items here and original Christmas gifts

definitions.text: They provided new items here and original Christmas gifts

indicators.note: the letters of new items here are provided in a different order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone brought novelties and the first-ever presents at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the Magi, while 'new items here' rearranges into the answer: the gifts were the very first Christmas presents.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the nativity story brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the newborn Jesus.

clue.text: Maroon thread

definitions.meaning: to maroon someone is to leave them stuck, abandoned on a shore
a single fibre or filament, as of hair or yarn

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a castaway is stranded, and a single filament of yarn is a strand.

clue.text: Everybody's playtime?

parts.note: a musical direction marking a passage where all the players of the orchestra perform together

explanation.walkthrough: 'playtime' suggests a school break; it is the time when every member of the orchestra plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term meaning all marks a passage for the whole ensemble.

clue.text: Sweet and perfect to order

definitions.meaning: the idiom ... order means perfectly neat and tidy

explanation.definitionFit: It is a classic baked dessert, and the phrase for impeccable tidiness uses it.

clue.text: Oil and vinegar is bound to help the wound

definitions.meaning: the mix poured over a salad

definitions.text: is bound to help the wound
definitions.meaning: a bandage or pad tied over an injury

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means tied on, like a bandage, not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad dressing is oil and vinegar; a wound dressing is the covering tied over an injury.

clue.text: One-sided view from a correspondent?

parts.note: sounds like a biased opinion, but is a picture card with the scene printed on one side only, sent by someone writing home

explanation.walkthrough: 'One-sided view' suggests prejudice; it is literally a view (a picture) on one side of a card, and the correspondent is a holidaymaker, not a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture card mailed home carries a scenic image on its front face and the message on its back.

clue.text: Badly set university course, that's plain

indicators.note: the word set is badly arranged, so its letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a well-known Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A complaint that a university syllabus has been poorly put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges SET into STE. PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a famous Oxford degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland, a type of plain found across Eurasia.

clue.text: Progress with amorous overtures?

parts.note: both moving forward and making romantic or sexual approaches to someone

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both to move ahead and to make romantic passes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to proceed forward and also to make a pass at someone romantically.

clue.text: Girl comes back with something useful

indicators.note: the girl's name comes back, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A daughter returns home bringing something handy with her.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable or helpful resource, a thing of use.

clue.text: They ask questions of pitmen after cutback

indicators.note: the pitmen come after the cut-back piece in the answer

parts.note: the word splits in two: a chopping tool, the axe, then back, so the tool's name is written backwards
pitmen are coal miners who work down a pit

explanation.surface: Inspectors question coal miners following a round of reductions at the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' looks like one noun, a reduction; it must be split into two words, the second telling you to reverse the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners are people who set tests and question candidates or witnesses.

clue.text: Repetition is, after all, Peter Piper's speciality

indicators.note: the repetition word is placed after the word all

parts.note: iteration means doing or saying something again, repetition

explanation.surface: Peter Piper, of the tongue-twister, is mostly a matter of saying the same thing again.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers: a nursery tongue-twister built on repeated P sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue-twister about the pickled peppers is the classic example of repeating initial consonant sounds.

clue.text: Like stories that can lead to novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of can lead to are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Telling tales can grow into writing a whole book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book; it is the adjective meaning new, signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal means based on or consisting of short personal tales rather than hard evidence.

clue.text: Case is essential up in Lincoln

indicators.note: the essential word goes in, inside, the president's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar first name

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is written backwards

parts.note: vital means essential

explanation.surface: A legal case is crucial to the city of Lincoln, or to the president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the synonym for essential, as the clue runs down the grid; 'Lincoln' is not the English city but the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is a noun case, expressing by, with or from.

clue.text: Winter sport Aussie cricketers are famous for?

definitions.meaning: riding a sled down snowy slopes
verbally taunting the batsman from the field to break concentration

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the word means taunting an opposing batsman, a practice Australian teams are notorious for.
explanation.definitionFit: It means riding a sledge in snow and, in cricket slang, insulting the batsman.

clue.text: Weighed out prescribed food?

parts.note: food measured on scales and laid down by a doctor, read as the healthy mix of nutrients one should eat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Weighed out' plays on the scales sense of balanced; 'prescribed food' is a regimen, a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A healthy eating plan with the right proportions of each food group is called this.

clue.text: Develop part of a revolver

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words a revolver, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Instructions to process film, or a component of a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually over time.

clue.text: Their function is to secure quiet in class

indicators.note: the quiet sign goes in, inside, the word class

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A teacher's job is to keep a classroom silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secure quiet' looks like a teacher keeping order; secure is the definition's verb, fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasps are fasteners, like those on a necklace or handbag, holding things shut.

clue.text: Wife of Perseus, wrongly named Dora

indicators.note: the words named Dora are put together wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has got the name of a mythical hero's wife wrong, calling her Dora.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Perseus rescued the princess chained to a rock as a sea monster's sacrifice, then married her.

clue.text: Once a rough expanse of water

indicators.note: the words once a are roughed up, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stretch of sea that was once choppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' seems to describe the sea; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is one of the great bodies of salt water covering the globe.

clue.text: He leads many to sin

indicators.note: the many letter leads, coming first before the sin word

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number, so many
evil means wickedness, sin

explanation.surface: A man who tempts lots of people into wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the Roman numeral 500, stands for 'many' here. The whole clue also describes Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the male tempter, so a pronoun for him works as the definition.

clue.text: Is about to get up, but flags

indicators.note: the word Is goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: to get up is to rise from bed

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get out of bed but their energy droops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' looks like a verb meaning tires; it is the noun, the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the iris plant, especially the yellow water iris.

clue.text: Nuts are found in them — and bolts

definitions.meaning: nuts here are small lumps of coal, kept in coal buckets by the fire
to bolt is to run off hurriedly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'bolts' suggest hardware, but nuts are pieces of coal and bolts means dashes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal bucket by the hearth holds lumps of coal, and to scurry away hastily is another sense.

clue.text: Motor found on fire, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a machine that produces power and drives a vehicle
the word follows fire in the name of the red emergency vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: 'found on fire' suggests something burning; it means the word comes after 'fire' in a compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine powering a car is called this, and it completes the firefighters' vehicle name.

clue.text: As an afterthought, changes the songbooks

parts.note: PS, postscript, is what one adds at the end of a letter as an afterthought
alters means changes

explanation.surface: Someone tacks on a late revision to the church hymnals.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books containing the psalms, sung in church services.
